harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ 4.3.5 cluster (node1/node2/node3, CentOS Stream 10) using the official RabbitMQ Cloudsmith el9 repos. Created a dedicated CA and per-node server certs; rabbitmq.conf enforces listeners.tcp=none / TLS-only AMQP on 5671 with ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, so only clients presenting a certificate issued by this CA are accepted (verified both positive and negative cases at the TLS layer and at the AMQP/pika protocol layer). Management HTTP API (15672) is bound to each node's own cluster IP (not 0.0.0.0-equivalent wildcard reachability) and firewalld restricts 15672/4369/25672 to the 10.100.195.0/24 cluster subnet only, while 5671 stays open for external AMQPS clients. guest user removed; a cluster_admin administrator account created. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id + healthy cluster/service state, issued systemd reboot (ack returned pre-disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified RabbitMQ active with full 3/3 running nodes and zero network partitions after each restart, only proceeding to the next node once the cluster was fully healthy.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 3 nodes (CentOS Stream 10, no prior RabbitMQ/Erlang) and confirmed outbound internet access
Fetched current RabbitMQ el9 Cloudsmith repo/signing-key instructions via WebFetch and applied them to all nodes
Installed erlang + rabbitmq-server + logrotate on node1/node2/node3 in parallel (backgrounded, polled logs to completion)
Set up passwordless inter-node SSH via CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY and populated /etc/hosts from CLUSTER_HOSTS

Generated a dedicated CA (RabbitMQ Cluster CA) plus per-node server certs (CN/SAN = node name + cluster IP) and a CA-signed client cert, all on node1; distributed CA cert + server cert/key to node2/node3 via scp with correct ownership (root:rabbitmq) and SELinux context (rabbitmq_conf_t)
Generated a shared Erlang cookie and distributed it to all three nodes for clustering

Wrote /etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf on each node: listeners.tcp=none, TLS-only AMQP on 5671 with verify_peer+fail_if_no_peer_cert, management.tcp.ip bound to each node's own IP, classic_config peer discovery listing all 3 nodes
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin (offline) on all nodes
Configured firewalld on all nodes: opened 5671/tcp publicly, restricted 15672/4369/25672 to 10.100.195.0/24 via rich rules
Started/enabled rabbitmq-server on all 3 nodes; verified automatic cluster formation (3/3 running, disk nodes, no partitions)
Created cluster_admin administrator user, deleted default guest user

Generated a rogue self-signed cert (not CA-signed) and used openssl s_client plus a Python/pika AMQPS test to prove: CA-signed client cert connects and can publish/consume; rogue cert is rejected with a TLS bad_certificate alert both at handshake and application level
Verified management API reachable (401 auth prompt) from a cluster peer and bound only to the node's own IP, not a wildcard address

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol sequentially on node1, node2, then node3: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline, issued a backgrounded systemd reboot so the ack returned first, polled until SSH/exec responded again, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified RabbitMQ service active with full 3-node cluster and zero partitions before proceeding to the next node
Re-verified TLS accept/reject behavior and firewalld persistence after all restarts completed
Cleaned up temporary test users/queues created for verification

evidence.requirement: RabbitMQ cluster spans node1, node2, node3
evidence.summary: cluster_status shows rabbit@node1/node2/node3 as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with no partitions, both at initial formation and after each restart

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA generated on node1 (openssl req -x509), per-node server certs signed by it, rabbitmq.conf sets listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671 with ssl_options pointing at the CA/server cert/key; cluster_status listeners show amqp/ssl on 5671 only

evidence.requirement: Only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted
evidence.summary: CA-signed client cert completes TLS handshake and successfully publishes/consumes an AMQPS message via pika; a self-signed (rogue) cert is rejected with tls_alert bad_certificate both in the RabbitMQ log and as a client-side SSLError, confirmed again after all node restarts

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: management.tcp.ip bound to each node's own cluster IP (not wildcard), firewalld rich rules restrict 15672/4369/25672 to 10.100.195.0/24, and a request from a cluster peer (node2) reaches the API (401) while firewall config persisted through reboot
Baseline boot_id 4cee4ea8...; reboot ack returned pre-disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to c2073cdd...; rabbitmq-server active/enabled; cluster back to 3/3 running nodes, no partitions
Baseline boot_id a70d7f83...; reboot ack returned pre-disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to 87a7d36b...; rabbitmq-server active and cluster shows 3/3 running nodes, no partitions
Baseline boot_id 984a7d52...; reboot ack returned pre-disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to 7de934fb...; rabbitmq-server active and cluster shows 3/3 running nodes, no partitions
